# ⛔ NOTE (arc 109) — the consumption wall found a REAL violation on its first run, in GENERATED code

**Filed 2026-08-21.** The param-spec consumption wall was built, and the first thing it did was
refuse the stdlib:

```
type parameter "K" in :wat::cache::lru-svc::Record's param-spec is declared but never used
```

**That declaration is not written anywhere.** `:wat::cache::lru-svc::Record` is generated by
`defservice` from `wat/cache.wat:195`'s `:durable [capacity <- :wat::core::i64]` — a record with
exactly one field, typed `i64`. It carries `<K,V>` because the macro stamps the SERVICE's full
param list onto every type it generates, needed or not.

★ **The wall is correct and the finding is real.** This is the same over-stamping β-ii-b already
deleted from 18 generated FUNCTION names; it reaches generated TYPES too. The difference is that
now there is a check that proves it rather than an argument that suggests it.

## ⚠ The limit of my corpus scan, stated so it is not repeated

I predicted zero violations from a scan of 38 parametric declarations. That scan read `.wat`
**source** for `defrecord :name<T>`. It structurally cannot see a declaration that exists only after
macro expansion. So the prediction was true and irrelevant — the violating declaration is never
written down.

Third instrument limit in one session: grep cannot see prose, cannot see string literals, and
cannot see generated code. `[[feedback_state_what_the_instrument_can_see_before_quoting_it]]`

## The shared-premise check, because it nearly went the other way

All the options rested on "`Record<K,V>` is a defect." It might have been deliberate: an unused param
**still discriminates** (measured — `Phantom<i64>` ≠ `Phantom<String>`), so stamping could be what
keeps `lru-svc<i64,String>`'s Record distinct from `lru-svc<String,i64>`'s.

**It is spurious here.** `lru-svc::Record` holds one field, `capacity <- i64`. Its contents do not
vary with `K` or `V`, so the two instantiations genuinely ARE the same type; sharing it is correct.
A phantom param would manufacture a distinction the data does not have. Premise holds.

## The ruling — four questions, three options

- **A — fix the over-stamping; the wall lands after, as A's own acceptance test.**
  Obvious YES · Simple YES (it REMOVES the unconditional stamp — the same deletion β-ii-b made for
  function names) · Honest YES (generated code obeys the language's rules, proven not trusted) ·
  Good UX YES. **4–0 — RULED.**
- **B — land the wall now, exempting generated declarations.** Obvious NO ("the rule applies unless
  a macro wrote it" must be known before a reader can predict legality) · Simple NO (needs a
  provenance flag nothing else wants, and every future check inherits the question) · **Honest NO**
  — it exempts precisely the code nobody reads, where an unreadable declaration does the most
  damage, and converts a real finding into a permanent blind spot. **Fails.**
- **C — abandon the wall; the stamping is deliberate.** Obvious NO · Simple YES · **Honest NO** —
  rests on a justification the premise check dissolves. **Fails.**

★ **A's decisive property: the wall becomes its own acceptance test.** Fix the stamping, and the
thing that proves the fix is the check that found the defect. There is no separate row to invent and
no way to declare it done while it is not.

## Where the work is parked

The wall's implementation is preserved as **`PATCH-param-spec-consumption-wall.patch`** in this
directory — 291 lines, applies to `src/runtime.rs`, `src/types.rs`, `src/types/error.rs`. The tree
is reverted and green; the patch re-applies once `defservice` stops over-stamping.

**It is NOT in the stash.** `stash@{0}` holds the lifecycle strike and is not to be disturbed.

### What the patch contains, verified by reading before it was parked

- **ONE walker.** `walk_free_type_vars` hoisted out of `collect_free_type_vars`; two entry points
  (`collect_free_type_vars` and the new `collect_free_type_vars_in`) share it. Zero new
  `Parametric{args}` recursions in `types.rs` — measured.
- **ONE check**, at `parse_type_decl`'s single return.
- **A new `TypeErrorKind::UnconsumedTypeParam`** whose message names the param, the declaration,
  both remedies, and states the not-vacuous framing.

★ **And the rider caught a defect in my brief that would have broken the wall.** DESIGN and BRIEF
both said Surface's members are its "fields". Measured: every parametric `defsurface` in the corpus
— `Seqable<T>`, `Dialable<S,R>`, `TypedCapability<S,R>`, `Cache<K,V>`, `Holds<T>`, `Pair<A,B>` —
declares **zero** plain field members and consumes its params exclusively through `:features` method
signatures. A wall reading only fields would have rejected every one of them. It wired `Method`
args + rest + ret instead and documented the discrepancy at the wiring site.
